content.title: About
content.content: Sushi roll with eel (Unagi) is a traditional Japanese dish consisting of rice, nori, sliced smoked eel and often drizzled with sweet unagi sauce. The eel has a delicate, slightly sweet flavor and a buttery texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eel is considered a delicacy in Japan and is often served on special occasions.
Traditional unagi sauce is made from soy sauce, sugar, mirin and sake, then caramelized.
Eel rolls are frequently garnished with sesame seeds and finely chopped green onions.
In Japan, eel is farm‑raised in specialized farms where they are fed a special diet to develop its characteristic taste.
Eel sushi is usually served warm, unlike most rolls which are served cold.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Eel provides EPA and DHA, which support heart and vascular health.

items.title: Source of high‑quality protein
items.content: Eel delivers complete animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamin B12 and niacin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Eel is a good source of potassium, magnesium and iron, supporting muscle function and blood formation.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Unagi sauce contains antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Unagi sauce is often salty, which can be an issue for people with hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Eel and the sweet sauce make the roll relatively high in calories, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to seafood may react to eel.

items.title: Potential parasites
items.content: Raw fish can harbor parasites; therefore eel is typically cooked before serving.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The roll is usually sliced into 6–8 pieces and eaten with chopsticks. It can be lightly dipped in soy sauce, but avoid overwhelming the delicate unagi flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sushi rolls in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for no more than 24 hours. For longer storage, freeze them, though the rice texture may change.
